targets.authors: Jenkins, J., Schulze, M., Marti, A., & Harbaugh, A. G.
targets.title: Curriculum-based measurement of reading growth: Weekly versus intermittent progress monitoring
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study was to replicate and extend the work of Jenkins et al. (2017), the findings of which could have broad implications for schools.
targets.outcome_quote: This study replicated and extended the work of Jenkins and colleagues by examining the accuracy and timeliness of different PM schedules for 51 students with disabilities. Results indicated that the accuracy and timeliness of the PM schedules for the current sample was poorer than the accuracy and timeliness reported by Jenkins and colleagues. In line with the results of the original study, however, these results indicated that intermittent PM schedules sufficiently predicted student true growth compared to weekly PM schedule.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm comparability of intermittent and weekly schedules, while explicitly contrasting poorer accuracy and slower threshold attainment with the original. The discussion statement of replicating conclusions is about the relative schedule comparison; it does not supersede these separately tested differences.
